Definition / Description: Cost of turnover for employees with less than one year of tenure as a percentage of the total turnover cost.
Formula: Total Termination Value.< 1-Year Tenure / Total Termination Value
Application / Measure: Staffing Effectiveness | Cost of low tenure employee attrition. Also as a measure of staffing effectiveness.
Commentary / Interpretation: Turnover Cost Rate—< 1-Year Tenure measures the percentage of termination costs that come from employees with less than one year of tenure. While this measure does not indicate whether turnover costs among low-tenure employees is high or low, it does indicate the extent to which the turnover costs are driven by low-tenure employees. A result of 40% means that 40% of all termination costs are from these low-tenure employees. Most organizations experience their highest turnover among low-tenure employees. Low-tenure terminations carry with them similar costs and productivity losses to other terminations. However, low-tenure terminations might also signal potential failures of recruiting and onboarding processes. Therefore, New Hire Turnover Contribution can help an employer to approximate the magnitude of turnover costs driven by recruiting and onboarding issues as compared to other potential turnover issues. The higher the result for this measure, the greater the volume of turnover costs that might be prevented through recruiting and onboarding improvement.

Definition / Description: Percentage of external hires receiving a sign-on bonus.
Application / Measure: Measurement of the usage of Sign-On Bonuses.

Definition / Description: Distribution of recruitment expenses by type, such as travel, advertising, compensation, etc. | Share of total recruiting expense by expense type.
Formula: (Recruitment Expense.[Type] / Recruitment Expense) * 100 | sum( expense_amount where type=T ) / sum( expense_amount )
Application / Measure: recruiting costs Isolating and wish to monitor the relative magnitude of direct costs, such as relocation allowances and agency fees.
Commentary / Interpretation: Recruitment costs include direct costs of filling positions, such as advertising costs, agency fees, travel reimbursement of candidates or interviewers, screening tests, and relocation allowances. Recruitment costs are also likely to include the overhead costs of running a recruiting function, such as the salaries of recruiters, the costs of maintaining a resume bank, the costs of sending communications or printing collateral, etc. In addition, recruitment expenses can include indirect productivity costs of hiring managers and other called upon to interview candidates, though such costs are difficult to quantify.
Notes: Useful for channel ROI and budget planning.

Definition / Description: Recruitment expense per hire, including internal and external hires. | Total recruitment expense divided by number of hires.
Formula: Recruitment Expense / Hires | sum( recruiting_expense ) / count( hires )
Application / Measure: Measurement of recruiting efficiency. |
Commentary / Interpretation: advertising costs, agency fees, travel reimbursement of candidates or interviewers, screening tests, and relocation allowances. Recruitment costs are also likely to include the overhead costs of running a recruiting function, such as the salaries of recruiters, the costs of maintaining a resume bank, the costs of sending communications or printing collateral, etc. In addition, recruitment expenses can include indirect productivity costs of hiring managers and other called upon to interview candidates, though such costs are difficult to quantify.
Notes: Break out by channel (ads, agency, tools, events).

Definition / Description: Average sign-on bonus received by external hires given a sign-on bonus.
Formula: Sign-On Bonus Expense / External Hires.Sign-On Bonus
Application / Measure: usage of sign-on bonuses

Definition / Description: Measures how consistently similar candidate profiles receive the same screening decision across reviewers. Why it matters: High variation indicates unstable application of judgment.

Measures how often screening decisions align with defined must-have criteria and scoring thresholds. Example: Candidate scores 82; threshold is 75; decision = Reject → misalignment. Why it matters: Ensures screening decisions reflect agreed standards.

Measures whether screening score bands meaningfully differentiate downstream candidate performance. Example: Strong band → 70% pass HM screen, Borderline → 35%, Weak → 10% = strong (equal rates across bands = weak signals | Why it matters: Indicates whether screening produces real signal or noise.
Estimates the likelihood that candidates meeting rubric criteria were rejected during screening. Why it matters: Identifies hidden talent loss.

Measures whether screening thresholds shift across time or reviewers. Example: Q1 threshold = 70, Q3 threshold = 80 → drift | Why it matters: Prevents silent tightening or loosening of standards. Indicates demand exceeds resources.
Rehires as a percentage of total external hires.
Application / Measure: Useful for organizations that have specific initiatives around rehires, such as alumni tracking processes or alumni networks.
Commentary / Interpretation: Rehire Rate indicates the percentage of external hires during the period that are former employees of the organization.

Definition / Description: Number of internal hires for every external hire.
Application / Measure: For one reason or another the organization may wish to tilt recruitment toward hiring internally or externally or may have a specific ratio in mind. Reasons include reducing recruitment expenses, increasing hiring quality, increasing retention rates, increasing internal development opportunities, etc.
Commentary / Interpretation: A recruitment ratio of four means that the organization has made four internal placements to vacant positions for every one external hire. Internal hires are often calculated to include all internal movements, such as transfers, promotions, and demotions.
Tags: reducing recruitment expenses, increasing hiring quality, increasing retention rates, increasing internal development opportunities, etc.

Definition / Description: Distribution of external hires by recruitment source, including referral, rehire, agency, etc.
Application / Measure: Determining the % of hiring by source. For one reason or another the organization may wish to tilt recruitment toward particular sources. Reasons may include reducing recruitment expenses, increasing hiring quality, increasing retention rates, etc.
Tags: reducing recruitment expenses, increasing hiring quality, increasing retention rates, etc.

Metric: New Position Recruitment Ratio (New role vs backfill)
Definition / Description: Ratio of new position hires to replacement hires, including internal and external hires.
Application / Measure: rate of change of job roles.
Commentary / Interpretation: New Position Recruitment Ratio compares the number of newly created positions to the number of replacement positions during a period. In other words, across all the organization's hires, how many are into new positions and how many are replacing people who have terminated or transferred out of existing positions? A result of this measure of .5 indicates there was one new position hire for every two replacement position hires during the period.

Metric: New Position Recruitment Rate (New role hires %of headcount)
Definition / Description: Hires into newly created positions (including internal and external hires), as a percentage of average headcount.
Application / Measure: rate of change of job roles.
Commentary / Interpretation: New Position Recruitment Rate shows the number of newly created positions in relation to the size of the workforce. A "new position" is not necessarily one for which the title and the role have never existed before filling a new position may mean expanding a group of four analysts to become five analysts, or it may mean creating a Marketing Analyst position whose title did not previously exist for the organization.

Definition / Description: The number of external hires for every termination during the reporting period.
Application / Measure: Monitoring headcount levels over time in support of cost management initiatives or growth strategies.
Commentary / Interpretation: Net Hire Ratio measures the total number of external hires that replace terminated employees.

Definition / Description: External hires as a percentage of average headcount during the reporting period.
Commentary / Interpretation: This measure is used to monitor "churn" of the workforce, the rate at which employees are entering the organization, and the hiring volume as an outcome of recruitment activities.

Definition / Description: Days from decision request created to decision logged in pilot functions.
Notes: Log decision type and escalation path.

Definition / Description: Share of HM actions (feedback/decisions) taken within SLA.
Notes: Show by team to target coaching.

Definition / Description: Distribution of interviews per interviewer vs. target range.
Formula: count( interviewer_weeks within target ) / count( interviewer_weeks )
Notes: Optional: show Gini coefficient alongside.

Definition / Description: Sum of meeting hours per FTE per week in pilot functions.
Notes: Use consistent working-hours definition.

Definition / Description: Share of scheduled interviews where the candidate or interviewer did not attend.
Formula: count( interview_status in {No Show, Canceled Late} ) / count( scheduled_interviews )
Notes: Track candidate vs interviewer separately.

Definition / Description: Share of submitted scorecards received within 24 hours of interview end.
Notes: Break out by HM vs panel to target nudges.

Definition / Description: Share of applications that progress to recruiter screen.
Notes:
Pass-throughs: Denominator = candidates who ENTERED the stage in the period; Numerator = those who LATER reached the next stage (allow lag across weeks).
Cohorting: Use apply week (App→Screen) and stage-entry week for all pass-through denominators; do not mix with event week.

Definition / Description: Share of final loops that result in an offer.
Notes:
Pass-throughs: Denominator = candidates who ENTERED the stage in the period; Numerator = those who LATER reached the next stage (allow lag across weeks).
Cohorting: Use apply week (App→Screen) and stage-entry week for all pass-through denominators; do not mix with event week.

Definition / Description: Share of HM interviews that progress to final loop.
Notes:
Pass-throughs: Denominator = candidates who ENTERED the stage in the period; Numerator = those who LATER reached the next stage (allow lag across weeks).
Cohorting: Use apply week (App→Screen) and stage-entry week for all pass-through denominators; do not mix with event week.

Definition / Description: Share of offers that result in a hire.
Notes:
Pass-throughs: Denominator = candidates who ENTERED the stage in the period; Numerator = those who LATER reached the next stage (allow lag across weeks).
Cohorting: Use apply week (App→Screen) and stage-entry week for all pass-through denominators; do not mix with event week.

Definition / Description: Share of screens that progress to HM interview.
Notes:
Pass-throughs: Denominator = candidates who ENTERED the stage in the period; Numerator = those who LATER reached the next stage (allow lag across weeks).
Cohorting: Use apply week (App→Screen) and stage-entry week for all pass-through denominators; do not mix with event week.

Definition / Description: Calendar days from application submission to offer acceptance (or hire) for filled requisitions.
Notes: If using 'hire_dt' instead of 'offer_accepted_dt', note in version.

Definition / Description: Hours from interview request creation to first scheduled interview start time.
Notes: Use UTC or local consistently.

Definition / Description: Referrals submitted divided by average headcount in period.
Formula: (Referrals / Average Headcount) * 100 | count( referrals ) / avg( headcount )
Application / Measure: Measurement of the Referral Program.
Notes: Segment by department and location.

Definition / Description: Referrals hired as a percentage of total referrals. | Hires from referrals divided by referrals submitted.
Formula: (External Hires.Referrals / Referrals) * 100 | count( referral_hires ) / count( referrals )
Application / Measure: Success of the Referral Program.
Notes: Add stepwise conversion: Referral→App, App→Screen, etc.

Definition / Description: Percentage of offers that were accepted.
Application / Measure: staffing effectiveness
Notes: Track reasons (expired/declined/withdrawn) as sub-dimensions.

Metric: Interviews to Hire Ratio (#Applicants) | Interviewee Ratio
Definition / Description: Average number of applicants interviewed for each internal and external hire. |Average number of interviews conducted for hired candidates.
Formula: Applicants.Interviewed / Offers.Accepted | count( interviews_for_hires ) / count( hires )
Application / Measure: one in a series that provides an indication of the proportion of candidates admitted through various gates in the recruiting process.
Notes: Break out by team/level; watch for panel duplication.

Definition / Description: Offers extended as a percentage of distinct applicants interviewed during the period. | Share of interviewed applicants who received an offer.
Application / Measure: one in a series that provides an indication of the proportion of candidates admitted through various gates in the recruiting process.
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, a result of 10% means that 10% of interviewed applicants received job offers.
Notes: Equivalent to Interview→Offer conversion.

Definition / Description: Average number of days elapsed between requisition date and start date for internal and external hires. | Average calendar days from offer acceptance to candidate start date.
Formula: Total days to Start / Hires | avg( start_dt - offer_accepted_dt )
Numerator: Sum of days from acceptance to start
Application / Measure: Staffing Timeliness
Notes: Track separately for relocations if needed.

Definition / Description: Average number of days elapsed between requisition date and offer acceptance for internal and external hires. | Average calendar days from requisition open (or approved) to offer acceptance for filled requisitions.
Formula: Total Days to Fill / Offers.Accepted | avg( offer_accepted_dt - req_open_dt )
Numerator: Total Days to Fill | Sum of days from open to offer acceptance
Application / Measure: Staffing Timeliness
Notes: If using 'posted_dt' instead of 'open_dt', note in version.

Definition / Description: Average number of interviews conducted with the hired candidate for each internal and external hire.
Application / Measure: Staffing Efficiency
Commentary / Interpretation: Average Interviews per Hire indicates, for each person hired within a period, how many interviews that person had before being hired. For example, a result of 5.5 means that people hired had an average of 5.5 interviews during the recruiting process.

Metric: Pass-through Ratio: Applicants --> Hire | Applicant Ratio
Definition / Description: Average number of applicants for each internal and external hire.
Application / Measure: Applicant screening resources required from a job applicant pool.
Commentary / Interpretation: One in a series that provides an indication of the proportion of candidates admitted through various gates in the recruiting process.

Definition / Description: Percentage of applicants that are interviewed during a period. | Share of applicants who were interviewed (any interview).
Application / Measure: Balance between interviewing "enough" candidates to provide a sufficient sampling of the qualified candidate pool and straining the recruiting process by interviewing an excessive number of candidates.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 20% means that 20% of all applicants are interviewed.
Notes: Equivalent to App→Interview pass-through.

Definition / Description: Terminations of short-tenure employees as a percentage of total terminations during the reporting period.
Application / Measure: employee turnover Analysis
Commentary / Interpretation: New Hire Turnover Contribution measures the percentage of terminations that come from “short-tenure” employees. While this measure does not indicate whether turnover among short-tenure employees is high or low, it does indicate the extent to which the turnover experienced by the organization comes from short-tenure employees. A result of 30% means that 30% of all terminations were of employees with short tenure.

Metric: On-Time Talent Delivery Factor (days per accepted offer)
Definition / Description: Average number of days that hired employee start dates differ from requisition need-by dates. | Average deviation in days between need-by date and offer acceptance date; negative = early, positive = late.
Formula: Total Days Deviation from Need-By Date / Offers.Accepted | avg( offer_accepted_dt - need_by_dt )
Numerator: Total Days Deviation from Need-By Date | Sum of (accepted_dt - need_by_dt)
Application / Measure: Staffing timeliness  measurement
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of -2,5 for On-Time Delivery Factor indicates that, on average, hires start two and a half days prior to their need-by dates. A result of 4.0 indicates that, on average, hires start four days after their need-by dates.
Notes: Report distribution (p50/p75/p90). A value >0 indicates late delivery.

Definition / Description: Terminations of low-tenure employees as a percentage of total hires during the reporting period. | Share of external hires who exit within 90 days of start.
Formula: (Terminations.Short Tenure / External Hires) * 100 | count( terminations_short_tenure ) / count( external_hires )
Application / Measure: staffing effectiveness.
Tags: As an alternative to viewing termination rates within various tenure levels, New Hire Tenure instead compares "short tenure" terminations to the number of external hires made within the period.
Notes: Define 'short tenure' window explicitly (e.g., ≤90 days).

Definition / Description: Relative measure of employee's engagement in their work.
Application / Measure: Measurement of employee engagement for purposes of predicting productivity and/or as a tool for analytically deriving the reasons for low engagement so they can be addressed before they lead to low productivity.
Commentary / Interpretation: Organizations typically measure employee engagement using survey results. Each survey will likely have a different set of questions or methodologies for measuring employee engagement. The Employee Engagement Index measures employees’ engagement with their jobs or day-to-day work. It is based on survey questions that assess factors such as the effort and enthusiasm they put into their daily activities. It is designed to measure the extent to which employees contribute their discretionary effort to the firm. Employee engagement is thus distinct from employee commitment, which measures attachment to the firm and views of the firm as a great place to work.

Definition / Description: Net Promoter Score from post-process survey on 0–10 scale.
Notes: Report separately by hired vs. not hired.

Definition / Description: An indication of how satisfied recent hires were with the recruiting process.
Application / Measure: Staffing Effectiveness Measure
Commentary / Interpretation: New Hire Satisfaction with recruiting represents a survey index or set of questions for recent hires to determine their satisfaction with the recruitment process.

Definition / Description: How well recent hires are performing within their positions.
Application / Measure: Staffing Effectiveness Measure
Commentary / Interpretation: New Hire Performance Satisfaction represents a survey index or set of questions posed to the managers of recent hires to determine the performance levels of those recent hires.

Metric: Absence Rate - Unscheduled by Days Worked (%of Work Time)
Definition / Description: Unscheduled Absence days a percentage of total workdays.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 3% means that unscheduled absences total 3% of all workdays. Put differently, a result of 3% means that, on an average day, 3 of every 100 employees are absent due to an unscheduled reason. This measure is an alternative measure of absence volume to Unscheduled Absence Days per Employee, providing a perspective by days worked rather than by employee. | Increase in unscheduled absence could indicate a job dissatisfaction problem – possibly supervisor or working conditions. Decrease in unscheduled absence could indicate a program to improve employee engagement, job satisfaction and motivation is working.
Tags: job dissatisfaction, program to improve employee engagement, job satisfaction and motivation is working.

Definition / Description: Average number of days of unscheduled absences per employee during the reporting period.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 1.5 means that, on average, each employee missed one and a half days of work during the period for unscheduled reasons. This measure is an alternative measure of absence volume to Unscheduled Absence Rate, providing a perspective by employee rather than by days worked. | Increase in unscheduled absence could indicate a job dissatisfaction problem – possibly supervisor or working conditions. Decrease in unscheduled absence could indicate a program to improve employee engagement, job satisfaction and motivation is working.

Definition / Description: Distribution of unscheduled absences by type, including sick leave, workplace injury, family leave, industrial dispute, etc.
Commentary / Interpretation: Unscheduled Absence Breakdown indicates the composition of unscheduled absence days that occurred during a period by the absence type. Graphically, the data are presented as a percentage of the total unscheduled absences, i.e., a stacked bar graph.

Definition / Description: Employees with a flexible work schedule as a percentage of total employees.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Flexible Work Schedule) / End of Period Headcount) *100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount.Flexible Work Schedule
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 10 indicates that 10% of the workforce participates in a flexible work arrangement and may not work the standard operating hours of the organization. | Compare productivity & engagement

Definition / Description: Paid time off hours taken as a percentage of those hours earned during the reporting period.
Application / Measure: Finance Forecasting, Staffing Resource Planning
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 80% means that for every 10 hours of PTO that employees accrue, they are only taking eight hours off.

Definition / Description: Average compensation cost of unscheduled absences per full-time equivalent employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, a result of $500 means that the compensation costs of employees’’ unscheduled absences, spread across all employees, averaged $500 per employee. Put differently, a result of $500 means that during the period, the organization paid $500 per FTE in compensation for unscheduled absences.

Definition / Description: Total days of employee absence as a percentage of total expected workdays during the reporting period.
Commentary / Interpretation: Absence Rate indicates the percentage of work time, expressed as workdays, that the average employee is absent for any reason during a period. A result of 3% means that absences total 3% of all workdays. Or, put differently, on an average day, 3 of every 100 employees are absent.

Metric: Benefits Expense Rate by %Total Comp Expense
Definition / Description: Benefits expense as a percentage of compensation and benefits expenses.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 30% indicates that benefits expenses compose 30% of the total amount an organization spends on employee compensation and benefits.

Definition / Description: A relative measure of employees’ satisfaction with the benefits provided by the organization.
Commentary / Interpretation: Benefits Satisfaction Index is a measure of employees’ overall satisfaction with benefits, such as medical insurance, dental insurance, disability insurance, child care, commuting, concierge, tuition reimbursement, or other benefit programs. Variations of this measure may present the results of individual survey questions (e.g., percentage of workforce rating medical benefits as “excellent”) or other subindexes of this overall satisfaction indicator.

Metric: Benefits Expense Rate by % Operating  Expense (%Org Cost)
Definition / Description: Benefits expense as a percentage of operating expense.
Commentary / Interpretation: Benefits Operating Expense Rate measures employee benefits costs (the organization’s portion) as compared to total operating expenses. A result of 5% means that benefits costs make up 5% of the organization’s total operating expenses.

Metric: Benefits Breakdown by Expense Type (%of Total)
Definition / Description: Organizational costs of employee benefits by type of benefit.
Commentary / Interpretation: Benefits Expense Type Breakdown provides the composition of benefits expense by various benefit types. Graphically, the data is presented as a percentage of the total Benefits Expense, i.e., a stacked bar graph.

Definition / Description: Average benefits expense (organization’s contribution) per full-time equivalent employee.
Average number of hours worked per week per employee
Formula: (Hours Worked / Number of Weeks) / Average Headcount
Commentary / Interpretation: Average Workweek measures the number of hours worked per week per employee, on average. A result of 37 means that the average person employed by the organization worked 37 hours per week during the period.

Definition / Description: The percentage of employees eligible to receive stock-based incentives.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Stock Incentive Eligible / End of Period Headcount) *100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount.Stock Incentive Eligible
Commentary / Interpretation: A value of 30 indicates that 30% of employees are eligible to receive stock-based incentives.

Definition / Description: Average number of stock options exercised per option-eligible employee.
Formula: Stock Options.Exercised / End of Period Headcount.Stock Option Eligible
Denominator: End of Period Headcount.Stock Option Eligible
Commentary / Interpretation: A value of 100 indicates that on average eligible employees exercised 100 stock options during the reporting period.

Metric: Stock Options Net Proceeds Per Employee ($Amount)
Definition / Description: Net proceeds to employees exercising stock options during the period for each employee who has exercised options.
Formula: Stock Option Net Proceeds / Headcount.Stock Option Eligible. Exercised
Commentary / Interpretation: Net Proceeds of Options per Employee Exercising indicates the average amount received by employees exercising options. The net proceeds are equal to the difference between sale price and strike price multiplied by the number of options exercised.

Metric: Stock Equity Incentive Value Per Employee
Definition / Description: The average value of equity incentives granted or earned per eligible employee.
Formula: Equity Incentive Value / Average Headcount.Equity Incentive Eligible
Commentary / Interpretation: Equity Incentive Value per Employee indicates the value of stock incentives granted to or earned by each eligible employee over the course of the period, using Black-Scholes or other valuation techniques. Stock incentives may include stock options, restricted stock, stock appreciation rights, performance shares, or other compensation related to equity. A value of $10,000 indicates that on average those eligible for an equity incentive received incentives valued at $10,000.

Definition / Description: The average number of stock options granted per eligible employee during the period.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 30 means that employees eligible to receive stock options received 30 options, on average, during the period.

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees receiving base salary increases during the reporting period.
Formula: End of Period Headcount.Base Salary Increase / End of Period Headcount * 100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount.Base Salary Increase

Definition / Description: Average total compensation expense, including direct, benefits, and equity compensation, per full-time equivalent employee.
Overtime expense as a percentage of total direct compensation expense.
Commentary / Interpretation: Overtime Rate measures the dollars of overtime paid relative to all forms of direct (cash) compensation paid. For example, a result of 10% indicates that overtime payments represent 10% of all cash payments to employees. By comparing overtime costs to all direct compensation costs, an organization can understand the impact of overtime on employees’ take-home pay and whether overtime costs represent an increasing or decreasing proportion of compensation over time.

Definition / Description: Average overtime cash compensation per full-time equivalent employee.

Metric: Compensation Ratio - Market Comparision (% to Other Orgs)
Definition / Description: Ratio of employees’ direct compensation to market-comparable direct compensation.
Formula: Direct Compensation Expense / Market Comparable Direct Compensation
Commentary / Interpretation: Market Compensation Ratio provides the ratio of direct (cash) compensation provided by the employer to that provided by a comparable market group. A result of 80% means that the organization’s compensation offerings are 80% of the offerings of other organizations. These data are sometimes provided only for certain components of direct compensation (e.g., base salary and bonus), and may not be available for all positions within an organization.

Definition / Description: Average direct compensation expense, including wages, bonus, and other cash compensation, per full-time equivalent employee.
Distribution of direct compensation by type, including base, overtime, bonus, incentives, etc.
Formula: (Direct Compensation Expense.[Compensation Type] / Direct Compensation Expense) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: Direct Compensation Breakdown provides the percentages of direct compensation paid that are of various compensation types. Graphically, the data are presented as a percentage of the total direct compensation, i.e., a stacked bar graph. Direct compensation, contrasted with benefits and equity compensation, relates to cash payments for base pay, variable pay, overtime, and other cash payments such as sign-on bonuses and relocation allowances.

Definition / Description: Direct compensation expenses as a percentage of operating expenses.
Commentary / Interpretation: Direct Comp Operating Expense Rate measures direct compensation (cash compensation such as wages and bonuses) as compared to total operating expenses. A result of 40% means that direct compensation makes up 40% of the organization’s total operating expenses.

Definition / Description: A relative measure of employees satisfaction with compensation.
Commentary / Interpretation: Compensation Satisfaction Index is a subjective measure of employees’ satisfaction with compensation packages. Among employee survey results, many organizations find that employees report low satisfaction with compensation. Though employers may not expect high results, the measure can be tracked over time to monitor in if satisfaction is increasing or decreasing. However, these survey results can be used to compare specific employee populations by division, location, job family, age group, performance level, etc.

Definition / Description: Employees receiving a bonus as a percentage of total employees eligible to receive a bonus.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Receiving Bonus / End of Period Headcount.Bonus Eligible) * 100
Application / Measure: Performance Evaluation, Finance Budgeting

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees eligible to receive a bonus.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Bonus Eligible / End of Period Headcount) * 100

Definition / Description: Bonus compensation as a percentage of all direct (cash) compensation.
Average actual bonus compensation received as a percentage of total potential bonus compensation.
Average total compensation expense, including direct, benefits, and equity compensation, per working hour.
Distinct employees submitting tuition reimbursement requests as a percentage of the workforce.

Metric: Staffing Rate - High Potential (% of Workforce)
Definition / Description: Percentage of the workforce designated as high potential.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.High Potential / End of Period Headcount) * 100

Metric: Staffing Rate - Graduate Degree (% of Workforce)
Definition / Description: Percentage of employees with a graduate degree or higher level of educational attainment.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Graduate Degree / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Application / Measure: Workforce characteristics - education level
Commentary / Interpretation: Staffing Rate—Graduate Degree indicates the percentage of the workforce that has attained a graduate degree (or equivalent advanced degree) or higher level of education. This measure, along with variations of this measure, can be useful in understanding the education levels of the workforce as a whole, as well as that of specific employee populations.

Definition / Description: Distribution of headcount by employees’ educational attainment, e.g., high school, university, advanced degree, etc.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.[Degree Level] / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Application / Measure: Workforce characteristics - education level
Commentary / Interpretation: Educational Attainment Breakdown depicts the percentages of the workforce that have reached various educational levels. Graphically, these data are presented as a percentage of the total workforce, i.e., a stacked bar graph. The measure provides information about the percentage of the workforce that has achieved a particular level of degree, as well as the overall distribution of educational attainment throughout the workforce.

Definition / Description: Percentage of eligible employees participating in development programs.
Formula: (Development Program Participants / End of Period Headcount.Eligible for Development Programs) * 100
Denominator: E#nd of Period Headcount.Eligible for Development Programs
Application / Measure: Development Program Participation %
Commentary / Interpretation: Such programs may relate to developing supervisory skills, acquiring multifunctional skills through rotations, participating in mentoring or networking, or other developmental activities. This measure provides an organization with a report of how extensively the eligible workforce participates in such programs.

Definition / Description: Average time required to satisfactorily resolve an employee grievance.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 60 means that an average of 60 calendar days elapsed between the filing and the resolution of grievances.

Definition / Description: The average number of grievances filed internally per employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 1% means that one grievance was filed for every 100 employees in headcount during the period.

Definition / Description: The average number of complaints to external agencies recorded per employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: External complaints are typically those filed with agencies such as, in the United States, OSHA or a state department of equal employment opportunity. Lawsuits filed by employees against the employer are also considered to be external complaints, as they are complaints requiring employer action toward an external party.

Metric: ADR - Alternative Dispute Resolution Success Rate
Definition / Description: Percentage of total internal grievances resolved that were settled through alternative dispute resolution processes.
Commentary / Interpretation: ADR Success Rate indicates the percentage of all employee internal resolved grievances that were resolved through an alternative dispute resolution (ADR) process. A result of 25% means that one of every four resolved grievances was resolved through ADR.

Definition / Description: Number of employees returning from disability leave for every resignation while on disability leave.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 3.0 means that the organization had three employees return to work from a disability leave for every one employee that terminated from a disability leave. A result less than one indicates that the employees that terminated from disability leave outnumbered those that returned to work.

Definition / Description: Workers compensation premium paid per full-time equivalent employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: Workers Compensation Premium per FTE measures the cost to the organization of workers compensation insurance relative to workforce size, whether the organization is self-insured or insured through external parties.

Definition / Description: Health and safety incidents that resulted in lost time per full-time equivalent employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of .10 indicates that the organization experienced one health and safety incident with lost time for every 10 full-time equivalent employees.

Definition / Description: Health and safety incidents per 100 full-time equivalent employees.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 3.0 means that the employer experienced 3 incidents for every 100 full-time equivalent employees. This is a commonly used measure for gauging workforce safety and is the primary safety measure captured for regulatory bodies.

Definition / Description: Health and safety incidents by type as a percentage of total health and safety incidents.
Commentary / Interpretation: H&S Incident Type Breakdown measures the composition of health and safety incidents by type of incident that occur during a period. Graphically, the data are. presented as a percentage of the total unscheduled absences, i.e., a stacked bar graph.

Definition / Description: Average occupational health & safety costs per employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of $1,000 means that the organization’s H&S costs equate to $1,000 for every full-time equivalent employee.

Definition / Description: Health and safety expense by type (prevention, rehabilitation, compensation, other) as a percentage of total H&S expense.
Commentary / Interpretation: H&S Expense Breakdown presents the composition of health and safety function expenses by type of expense that occur during a period. Graphically, the data are presented as a percentage of the total function expenses, i.e., a stacked bar graph.

Metric: Time Lost Average Per H&S Incident
Definition / Description: Average working days lost per health and safety incident.
Commentary / Interpretation: Average Time Lost per H&S Incident measures the average number of working days lost per health and safety incident and gives an indication of the severity of incidents occurring within the workplace. It may also be an indicator of the effectiveness of safety programs, procedures, training, and protective equipment.

Definition / Description: The percentage of calls answered within a specified number of seconds.
Formula: Calls Answered Within Specified Seconds / Total Calls * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, an employer may target employee service centers to answer 80% of calls within 20 seconds. The Service Level metric might report that 67% calls were actually answered within 20 seconds.

Definition / Description: HR transactions conducted via self-service as a percentage of the total number of HR transactions.
Formula: (HR Transactions Conducted via Self-Service / Number of HR Transactions) *100

Metric: Contact Center - One Call Resolution RAte
Definition / Description: Percentage of contact center transactions resolved within one call.
Formula: (Contacts Resolved in One Call / Total Contacts) * 100

Definition / Description: A relative measure of employee satisfaction with the contact center.
Commentary / Interpretation: Contact Center Satisfaction represents a survey index or set of questions for employees who have contacted the employee service center. Questions survey employees’’ satisfaction with their contact center experience.

Definition / Description: The average agent work time per call.
Percentage of HRIT transactions that are entered late.
Commentary / Interpretation: HRIT Late Transaction Rate indicates the percentage of HRIT transactions that are entered after the prescribed target period. The target period for entering transactions may be based on a specified number of days after an action or on a month-end or quarter-end close date. A result of 5% would indicate that 5% of all HRIT transactions are entered “late.”

Definition / Description: Average days elapsed from action occurrence to HRIT transaction entry.
Formula: Total Days to Entry / HRIT Transactions
Commentary / Interpretation: Total days to entry is the time that it takes for an HR transaction to be entered into the HRIS. For example, if a job transfer occurs on the 1st of a month and the transaction is entered on the 10th, the elapsed days to entry is nine days. Average Days To Entry is the average of all transactions in a measurement period.

Definition / Description: HR technology expense as a percentage of total organization technology expense.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 10% means that HR technology expenses make up 10% of total technology expenses.

Definition / Description: Average revenue per human resources full-time equivalent employee.
Application / Measure: This measure will only apply to organizations that operate HR as a “profit center” function within the organization. Under this model, the rest of the organization must purchase certain HR services it wants or needs.
Commentary / Interpretation: HR Revenue per HR Employee represents the amount of revenue produced internally by the human resources function per HR employee for its services to the organization.

Definition / Description: HR revenue as a proportion of total HR expenses.
Application / Measure: This measure will only apply to organizations that operate HR as a “profit center” function within the organization. Under this model, the rest of the organization must purchase certain HR services it wants or needs.
Commentary / Interpretation: HR Revenue Expense Rate represents the amount of revenue produced internally by the human resources function for its services to the organization, as compared to the operating costs of the HR function. A result of 70% indicates that HR revenues cover 70% of the function’s operating expenses.

Definition / Description: HR expense as a percentage of all operating expenses.
Commentary / Interpretation: HR Operating Expense Rate measures the percentage of total operating expenses that are attributed to the HR function. This measure indicates the organization’s relative investment in the HR function as compared with other operating activities. A result of 2%, for example, means that HR expenses represent 2% of the organization’s total operating expenses.

Definition / Description: HR expense per full-time equivalent employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: HR Expense per FTE measures the expenses associated with operating the HR function (including outsourcing costs) relative to the size of the workforce and indicates the relative investment in the HR function by the organization. A result of $3,000 means that HR expenses equate to $3,000 per full-time equivalent employee.

Definition / Description: Distribution of HR expense by expense type.
Commentary / Interpretation: Graphically, the data are presented as a percentage of total HR expenses, i.e., a stacked bar graph. Included in this metric are expenses from those functions that have an identifiable organizational connection to the Human Resources department. The expense types that constitute HR operating expenses would include: Compensation and Benefits of HR Staff, Training Investment for HR Employees, Facilities and Overhead, Travel Expenses, Technology, Outsourcing, Consultancy, Agency Costs

Definition / Description: Distribution of HR expense by HR function.
Commentary / Interpretation: Graphically, the data are presented as a percentage of total HR expenses, i.e., a stacked bar graph. Included in this metric are expenses from those functions that have an identifiable organizational connection to the Human Resources department. Expenses might include staff compensation and benefits, travel, technology, training, and other operating costs. HR functions may be considered in terms of “core” and “noncore.”  Core HR functions, those that typically fall into HR’’s area of responsibility, include: Compensation and Benefits, Staffing/Recruiting, Learning and Development, Generalists/Line Support, Industrial and Employee Relations, HR Policy, Strategy, and Organization Development, HR Function Management and Administration | Noncore functions, those that frequently report through other organizational areas, include: Payroll, Diversity, performance management, HR information management, occupational health and safety

Definition / Description: HR full-time equivalent employees as a percentage of total organization full-time equivalent employees.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 1% indicates that, on a full-time equivalent basis, one out of every one hundred employees is assigned to the HR function.

Definition / Description: Number of total organization employees per HR full-time equivalent employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: Number of total organization employees per HR full-time equivalent employee.

Definition / Description: Percentage breakdown of HR employees by HR functional area.
Formula: (HR End of Period Headcount.[Function] / HR End of Period Headcount) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: HR Staffing Breakdown provides the percentages of the Human Resources workforce within each HR function, such as recruitment, compensation and benefits, learning and development, payroll, generalist/line support, etc. HR function is based on the work the employee supports, which may or may not correspond precisely to organizational units. Graphically, the data are presented as a percentage of the total HR workforce, i.e., a stacked bar graph.

Definition / Description: Ratio of internal hires to external hires into the HR function.
Formula: HR Internal Hires / HR External Hires
Commentary / Interpretation: An HR Recruitment Source Ratio of 3 means that the HR function has made 3 internal appointments to vacant positions for every 1 external hire.

Definition / Description: Number of HR clerical and operative full-time equivalent employees for every one HR managerial and professional full-time equivalent employee.
Formula: HR FTE.Clerical & Operative / HR FTE.Managerial & Professional

Definition / Description: Transfers and promotions of HR employees as a percentage of the HR workforce.
Formula: (HR Promotions + HR Transfers) / HR Average Headcount * 100
Application / Measure: Understanding the extent to which HR is developing its own employees.
Commentary / Interpretation: An HR Mobility Rate of 10% means that 10% of employees in the HR function have transferred or been promoted within the period.

Definition / Description: Promotions as a percentage of all internal movements, which include promotions, transfers, and demotions.
Application / Measure: Rate of promotion, relative to other movements, for purposes of workforce planning that may include talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.
Commentary / Interpretation: An Upward Mobility result of 40% means that 40% of internal movements for the period were promotions, while the other 60% were transfers and demotions.
Tags: talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, attrition reduction.

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees that were transferred during the reporting period.
Application / Measure: Internal employee movement for purposes of Workforce Planning that may include talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.
Commentary / Interpretation: Transfer Rate indicates the percentage of the workforce that has experienced a transfer action during the period. For example, a Transfer Rate of 20% means that 20% of employees in the organization have transferred internally within the period.
Tags: talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.

Definition / Description: Average position tenure, in years, prior to promotion.
Formula: Total Position Tenure Prior to Promotion / Promotions
Numerator: Total Position Tenure Prior to Promotion
Application / Measure: Measurement of promotions for purposes of workforce planning that may include talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.
Commentary / Interpretation: Promotion Speed Ratio indicates, for employees that were promoted during the period, their average tenure in position prior to promotion. For example, an employee promoted two years after being hired into a position has a Promotion Speed Ratio equal to two years.
Tags: talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees that were promoted during the reporting period.
Application / Measure: Measurement of promotions for purposes of workforce planning that may include talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, a Promotion Rate of 5% means 5% of employees in the organizations have received promotions within the reporting period.
Tags: talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.

Definition / Description: Transfers as a percentage of all internal movements, including transfers, promotions, and demotions.
Application / Measure: Measurement of lateral movement across the organization for purposes of workforce planning that may include talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.
Commentary / Interpretation: A Lateral Mobility result of 40% means that 40% of internal movements for the period were transfers, while the other 60% were promotions or demotions.
Tags: talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.

Metric: Internal Placement Rate (% of Open Reqs)
Definition / Description: Internal hires as a percentage of total hires.
Application / Measure: Measurement of strategies involving the mix of internal versus external hires for purposes of workforce planning that may include talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.
Commentary / Interpretation: An internal Placement Rate of 60% means that 60% of the organization's appointments to vacant positions were from internal talent rather than from external hires.
Tags: talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, time to fill, or attrition reduction.

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees that moved internally during the reporting period, including transfers, promotions, or demotions.
Application / Measure: Measurement of the movement of internal talent for purposes of workforce planning that may include talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, or time to fill.
Commentary / Interpretation: Internal hire rate indicates the percentage of the workforce that has moved internally during the period. Internal movements are those resulting from employees' internal job changes within the organization, whether through actions of transfer, promotion, or demotion. For example, an internal hire rate of 40% means that 40% of employees in the organization have experienced one of these movements within the period.
Tags: talent development, quality of hire, cost reduction, or time to fill.

Definition / Description: Movements between functions as a percentage of total internal movements.
Application / Measure: Measurement of developmental programs that focus on building cross- functional opportunities for leadership development or skill broadening.
Commentary / Interpretation: Cross-Function Mobility indicates the percentage of internal movements that involve employees moving from one functional area to another, such as from Finance to Marketing or from Sales to Operations. Internal movements are those resulting from an employee's internal job changes within the organizations, regardless of function, whether through transfer, promotion, or demotion. A Cross-Function Mobility result of 40% means that 40% of internal movements for the period involved moves from one function to another, while the other 60% were movements within a function.

Definition / Description: Number of employees internally promoted for every employee internally transferred to a new position.
Application / Measure: To gauge the success of internal development of managers, performance management process controls, or other workforce planning.
Commentary / Interpretation: Career Path Ratio indicates the ratio of promotions to transfers that occurred within a period. A Career Path Ratio of .5 (i.e, a ratio of 1:2) means that there were two transfers for each promotion that occurred within the period.

Definition / Description: Relative measure of the growth rate of the succession pool.
Formula: ((Headcount.Successor Pool – Headcount.Successor Pool.Prior Year) / Headcount.Successor Pool.Prior Year) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: The Successor Pool Growth Rate establishes the percentage increase in headcount of the succession pool over the previous year. A result of 5% indicates that the current successor pool is 5% larger in size than it was last year.

Definition / Description: Average number of employees in the managerial succession pool per manager.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Successor Pool / End of Period Headcount.Manager.Succession-Applicable) *100
Commentary / Interpretation: Successor Pool Coverage measures the number of successors in the successor pool compared to the number of managers in the organization for whose positions require succession management focus. A result of 100% indicates that there are as many potential successors as there are managerial positions in need of potential successors.

Definition / Description: Percentage of managerial positions that do not have “ready” candidates identified for potential succession.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Manager.Succession-Applicable.No Ready Candidate / End of Period Headcount.Manager.Succession-Applicable) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: Positions Without Ready Candidates Rate indicates the percentage of managerial positions that require succession management focus but do not have a “ready” candidate identified. A result of 20% means that 20% of succession-applicable managerial positions do not have successor candidates identified that are ready to assume the position immediately if needed.

Definition / Description: A relative measure of employees’ perceptions of manager quality.
Commentary / Interpretation: Each survey will likely have a different set of questions or methodologies for measuring manager quality. The Manager Quality Index measures aggregate employee satisfaction with direct managers. The index is based on employee satisfaction with managers along multiple dimensions, including factors such as knowledge, skill, and personality. Although it provides an aggregate measure of manager quality, the index can also be disaggregated to identify those dimensions along which managers are particularly strong or weak.

Definition / Description: The percentage of employees who have had more than one manager within the most recent 12 months.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.>1 Supervisor in Previous 1-Year Period / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount.>1 Supervisor in Previous 1-Year Period
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 30% means that 30% of employees have had a change in direct supervisor within the past year.

Metric: LDP - Leadership Dev Plan Prevalence Rate
Definition / Description: Percentage of managers with Leadership Development Plans in place.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Manager.LDP / End of Period Headcount.Manager) *100
Commentary / Interpretation: LDPs might contain planned or recommended steps for a leader related to executive coaching, training courses, supervisory experience, experience in new functions or business lines, mentoring, and other key developmental areas. The plan is targeted toward the leadership competencies or personal skills that have been identified as in need of improvement or generally beneficial to all leaders.

Definition / Description: Gauge of employee satisfaction with organizational leaders
Commentary / Interpretation: Employee Satisfaction with Leadership represents a survey index or set of questions for employees to express their satisfaction with the organization’s leadership. Such a measure or index may be titled differently, depending on the survey used. While the measure called Manager Quality Index relates to employees’ opinions of their direct managers, Employee Satisfaction with Leadership looks more broadly at employees’ opinions about the leadership of their business line, function, and area, as well as the leadership of the organization as a whole. The opinions solicited from relevant survey questions typically relate to leaders’ competencies and skills (e.g., communication, subject mastery, employee development, personality, decision making), their ability to inspire confidence and trust and motivate performance, and the appropriateness of the business strategy being pursued.

Definition / Description: Internal movements of managers between functions as a percentage of total internal movements of managers.
Research and development (R&D) expense as a percentage of total operating expense.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 10% means that R&D expenses represented 10% of the organization’s total operating expenses

Metric: New Products & Services Revenue Per FTE
Definition / Description: Average new products and services operating revenue per full-time equivalent employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: New Products and Services Revenue per FTE indicates the dollar amount of revenue generated specifically by new products and services, relative to the size of the workforce. New Products and Services Revenue is a subset of Operating Revenue, relating only to specific products and services.

Definition / Description: Average market capitalization per full-time equivalent employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: Market capitalization, equal to the market price of stock shares multiplied by the number of shares outstanding, is considered one measure of a firm’s worth. It is essentially the value that the market places on the company, including both tangible assets listed on a balance sheet, as well as intangible assets such as brand name and workforce talent.

Definition / Description: Average intangible market value per full-time equivalent employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: The difference between the value that the market places on the firm’’s worth (market capitalization) and the book value of the firm’s assets represents the intangible assets of the organization. Such off-balance sheet assets include the product/service brand, the employment brand, the skills or characteristics of the workforce, or the intellectual property (including products, knowledge, tools, and processes) of the firm.

Definition / Description: Percentage of company stock owned by employees.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 15%, for example, indicates that 15% of the company’’s outstanding shares are held by employees.

Definition / Description: Corporate operating expense as a percentage of total operating expense.
Commentary / Interpretation: Corporate Expense Rate indicates the percentage of the organization’s operating expenses allocated to corporate functions, typically housed within a corporate office or corporate organizational unit. Corporate functions typically include HR, finance, legal, information technology, marketing, investor relations, corporate communications, facilities, real estate, procurement, and other functions that are essentially shared by the various business lines of the organization.

Definition / Description: Number of relevant work units produced per full-time equivalent employee during this period.
Commentary / Interpretation: The implementation of this measure will differ from industry to industry, and even potentially from organization to organization, based on the types of products or services the employer produces. For a manufacturer, this measure could include the number of cars, pipe fittings, reams of paper, or cans of paint produced. For a financial services or other services firm, this measure could reflect the number of loans originated, policies issued, hours billed, or contracts written.

Definition / Description: Volume of completed standard work items per FTE per week.
Notes: Normalize by complexity if available.

Metric: ROI - Return on Human Investment Ratio
Definition / Description: Operating profit returned for every dollar invested in employee compensation plus benefits.
Other labor costs as a percentage of total operating expense.
Commentary / Interpretation: Other Labor, sometimes called contingent labor, is the workforce used by the organization to generate its revenue and profit but not represented as employees with a reporting system such as an HRIS.

Definition / Description: Average operating revenue per full-time equivalent employee.
Average operating profit (before tax, interest, and depreciation) per full-time equivalent employee.
Average operating expense per full-time equivalent employee
Ratio of operating profit, adding back total compensation expense, returned for every dollar invested in employee compensation and benefits.
Formula: (Operating Profit + Total Compensation Expense) / Total Compensation Expense

Definition / Description: Average payroll expense per employee.
Percentage of paychecks processed in which an error occurred.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 3% means that, on average, 3 out of every 100 paychecks contains an error.

Definition / Description: Percentage of paychecks processed in which an overpayment occurred.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 2% means that, on average, 2 out of every 100 paychecks includes an overpayment.

Definition / Description: Average value of overpayments for the reporting period
Percentage of eligible managers whose performance is appraised using an upward review.
Application / Measure: Measurement of compliance with a Performance Appraisal Process.
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, a result of 70% means that 70% of the employees eligible to receive an upward review actually received one.

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees whose performance is appraised using a self-review.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Self Reviews / End of Period Headcount.Eligible for Self Review) * 100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount Self Reviews
Denominator: End of Period Headcount.Eligible for Self Review
Application / Measure: Measurement of compliance to the Performance Appraisal process.
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, a result of 70% means that 70% of the employees eligible to complete a self review actually completed one.

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees whose total compensation is at least in part dependent on individual performance.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Performance Contingent Compensation / End of Period Headcount) * 100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount.Performance Contingent Compensation
Application / Measure: Measurement of the penetration of performance-based pay.
Commentary / Interpretation: Performance contingent pay can be wage or bonus compensation that is dependent on individual performance.

Definition / Description: Ratio of the direct compensation (cash compensation) of high performers to the direct compensation of non-high performers.
Formula: Average Direct Compensation.High Performers / Average Direct Compensation.Non-High Performers
Application / Measure: Measuring the pay differential by performance.
Commentary / Interpretation: Performance-Based Pay Differential answers the question, “How much more do high performers earn than others?” It does so by comparing the direct compensation, including wages, bonus, and other cash compensation, of high performers to that of non-high performers. A result of 1.5 indicates that high performers earn $1.50 of direct compensation for every $1.00 earned by non–high performers.

Definition / Description: Distribution of performance appraisal occurrences by appraisal rating.
Application / Measure: Measurement of the Performance Rating Distribution. Useful for comparing one employee segment to another.
Commentary / Interpretation: Performance Rating Distribution provides the percentages of performance appraisal occurrences that result in various ratings. Graphically, the data are presented as a percentage of Performance Appraisal Participants, i.e., a stacked bar graph.

Definition / Description: Percentage of eligible employees who have received a performance appraisal during the reporting period.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Appraisal Eligible.Performance Appraisal / End of Period Headcount.Appraisal Eligible) * 100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount.Appraisal Eligible.Performance Appraisal
Application / Measure: Measurement of compliance to the Performance Appraisal process.
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, a result of 80% means that 80% of eligible employees actually received an appraisal during the period.

Definition / Description: Employees whose performance is appraised in part through peer reviews as a percentage of eligible employees.
Formula: (End of Period Headcount.Peer Review / End of Period Headcount. Eligible for Peer Review) * 100
Numerator: End of Period Headcount. Peer Review
Denominator: End of Period Headcount. Eligible for Peer Review
Application / Measure: Measurement of compliance with the performance appraisal process.
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, a result of 70% means that 70% of the employees eligible to receive a peer review actually received one. Results will tend to vary based on whether the practice is considered to be a mandatory component of the performance review process or a voluntary practice that may be instituted by individual managers. High results for this measure indicate that there are high compliance or adoption rates for the peer review practice.

Definition / Description: Percentage of performance appraisal participants whose rating improved to a “high” rating from a previous rating that was less than “high.”
Formula: (Performance Appraisal Participants.Rating High / Performance Appraisal Participants.Previous Rating Non-High) * 100
Application / Measure: Measurement of Performance Appraisal Upgrades for purposes determining the effectiveness of the performance appraisal system, identifying managers able to effect high levels of employee performance improvement, and/or successful employee development efforts.

Definition / Description: Percentage of performance appraisal participants receiving a higher rate than the previous rating.
Formula: (Performance Appraisal Participants.Rating Increase / Performance Appraisal Participants) * 100
Application / Measure: Measurement of Performance Appraisal Upgrades for purposes determining the effectiveness of the performance appraisal system and/or employee development efforts.
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, a result of 15% means that 15% of employees received a higher rating in the current period than in their previous appraisal. When performance is accurately assessed and ratings are accurately applied, this measure can offer an indication of whether employees are improving their performance and where pockets of improved performance can be found. Management may also find it useful to monitor rating increases because of their effects on bonus or other compensation plans, or any other programs linked to performance ratings.

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees receiving a poor performance rating at their preceding review whose rating increased during the period.
Formula: (Performance Appraisal Participants.Previous Rating Low.Rating Increase / Performance Appraisal Participants.Previous Rating Low) * 100
Numerator: Performance Appraisal Participants.Previous Rating Low.Rating Increase
Application / Measure: Measurement of the organizations ability to improve poor performance using the performance appraisal system and/or specific employee development initiatives.
Commentary / Interpretation: For example, a result of 20% indicates that 20% of employees who were low-rated at their previous review received a non-low rating at their most recent review. Assuming performance ratings are judged and applied accurately, this measure provides an indication of the improvement an organization is able to effect in low performers. Turnarounds may be attributed to changes employees make in their own performance, changes driven by managerial focus and coaching, changes driven by training, or a combination of these.

Definition / Description: Average performance appraisal rating of performance appraisals delivered during the period.
Formula: Total Performance Appraisal Rating / Performance Appraisal Occurrences
Application / Measure: Useful when comparing the performance of different employee segments.
Commentary / Interpretation: This measure indicates the mean performance appraisal rating for all performance appraisal participants in the reporting period. Organizations that give qualitative performance ratings (e.g., Meets, Exceeds) must convert each rating to a numeric equivalent to calculate an average.

Definition / Description: Training expense as a percentage of total compensation expense.
Number of employees for every full-time equivalent training function employee.
Commentary / Interpretation: A result of 1,000 means that there are 1,000 employees in the organization for every full-time equivalent training staff member.

Definition / Description: A relative measure of the effectiveness of training courses.
Commentary / Interpretation: Training Quality presents a gauge of the effectiveness of training. While individual organizations may use various survey instruments to assess Training Quality, a commonly used approach is that developed by Donald Kirkpatrick in the late 1950s. Under the Kirkpatrick approach, Training Quality may be assessed at any of four progressive levels. Survey instruments, assessments, tests, and other tools may be used to develop an index for Training Quality at any or all of these levels for various training courses. Level One: Reaction—Measures trainees’ satisfaction with aspects of the training program, including topic, speaker, schedule, etc. Level Two: Learning—Measures the knowledge trainees acquire during the program, including skills improved, attitudes changed, etc. Level Three: Behavior—Measures the extent to which participants change their behavior on the job as a result of knowledge they acquire during training. Level Four: Results—Measures the results of training programs, including higher productivity, improved quality, increased sales, larger profits, reduced turnover, and reduced costs.

Definition / Description: Percentage of employees completing specific course or content training.
Formula: ((Employees Completing Course(s) / Total Employees to Be Trained)) * 100
Commentary / Interpretation: Training Penetration Rate measures the percentage of employees completing a course or a content area of training. For example, an organization might measure the percentage of employees that have taken any courses related management development. For this purpose a Training Penetration Rate of 80% indicates that 80% of employees eligible to take a management development course have done so.

Definition / Description: Average number of training hours per training occurrence.
Average number of training hours per full-time equivalent employee.
Average training expense per employee.
Distribution of training courses by content type.
Formula: (Distinct Courses Offered.[Content Type] / Distinct Courses Offered) * 100
Application / Measure: This breakdown measure can help an organization better understand where training resources are focused and what types of courses are emphasized.
Commentary / Interpretation: Training Course Content Breakdown provides the percentages of various content types of distinct courses offered, such as technical, managerial, customer service, orientation, product, leadership development, or other relevant categorizations.

Definition / Description: Breakdown of training course offerings by delivery type, e.g., classroom, e-learning, etc.
Formula: (Distinct Courses Offered.[Delivery Type] / Distinct Courses Offered) * 100

Definition / Description: A relative measure of employees’ satisfaction with the training function.
Commentary / Interpretation: Employee Satisfaction with Training represents a survey index or set of questions for employees to determine their satisfaction with the quality and effectiveness of the training function. Such a measure or index may be titled differently, depending on the survey used. Survey questions may ask employees about satisfaction with particular courses, with particular curriculum areas or delivery types, or with the training function as a whole. Employees’ satisfaction levels with the training function typically represent a mixture of perceptions of quality of training, quality of instructors, breadth of training available, convenience, and value received. Training satisfaction surveys are typically administered either at the conclusion of a course or in an HR-related or general employee survey.

Definition / Description: Percentage of courses begun, but not completed, using learning technologies.
Average class size | Average number of employees trained per class offered.
Cost of turnover for employees with less than one year of tenure as a percentage of the total turnover cost.
Formula: Total Termination Value.< 1-Year Tenure / Total Termination Value
Application / Measure: Staffing Effectiveness | Cost of low tenure employee attrition. Also as a measure of staffing effectiveness.
Commentary / Interpretation: Turnover Cost Rate—< 1-Year Tenure measures the percentage of termination costs that come from employees with less than one year of tenure. While this measure does not indicate whether turnover costs among low-tenure employees is high or low, it does indicate the extent to which the turnover costs are driven by low-tenure employees. A result of 40% means that 40% of all termination costs are from these low-tenure employees. Most organizations experience their highest turnover among low-tenure employees. Low-tenure terminations carry with them similar costs and productivity losses to other terminations. However, low-tenure terminations might also signal potential failures of recruiting and onboarding processes. Therefore, New Hire Turnover Contribution can help an employer to approximate the magnitude of turnover costs driven by recruiting and onboarding issues as compared to other potential turnover issues. The higher the result for this measure, the greater the volume of turnover costs that might be prevented through recruiting and onboarding improvement.

Definition / Description: The value of all terminations during the period per full-time equivalent employee.
Application / Measure: Employee turnover cost
Commentary / Interpretation: Termination Value per FTE represents the cost of all terminations to the organization, relative to workforce size. Employee terminations can carry direct costs as well as efficiency and productivity costs or customer service deterioration. Direct costs include departure costs (e.g., accrued vacation), vacancy costs (e.g., temporary replacement help, recruiting advertising), and new hire costs (e.g., screening, relocation, increased salary over previous employee). Other costs can include decreased morale, lost productivity while peers “cover” the vacancy, the lost productivity of recruiters and hiring managers for recruiting a replacement, and the ramp-up time to productivity required for the replacement employee.

Definition / Description: The average value of each voluntary termination during the reporting period.
Application / Measure: Employee turnover cost
Commentary / Interpretation: Average Voluntary Termination Value represents the average cost of an Individual voluntary termination to the organization. Employee terminations can carry direct costs as well as efficiency and productivity costs or customer service deterioration. Direct costs include departure costs (e.g., accrued vacation), vacancy costs (e.g., temporary replacement help, recruiting advertising), and new hire costs (e.g., screening, relocation, increased salary over previous employee). Other costs can include decreased morale, lost productivity while peers “cover” the vacancy, the lost productivity of recruiters and hiring managers for recruiting a replacement, and the ramp-up time to productivity required for the replacement employee.

Definition / Description: The average value of each termination during the reporting period.
Application / Measure: Employee turnover cost
Commentary / Interpretation: Average Termination Value represents the average cost of an individual Termination to the organization. Employee terminations can carry direct costs to an organization, as well as efficiency and productivity costs or customer service deterioration. Direct costs generally include departure costs (e.g., accrued vacation), vacancy costs (e.g., temporary replacement help, recruiting advertising), and new hire costs (e.g., screening, relocation, increased salary over previous employee). Other costs can include decreased morale, lost productivity while peers “cover” the vacancy, the lost productivity of recruiters and hiring managers for recruiting a replacement, and the ramp-up time to productivity required for the replacement employee.

Definition / Description: Relative measure of employees' perceptions of offer fit with the organization.
Application / Measure: Degree of alignment between the organization’s value proposition and the values, or preferences, of employees. In aggregate, the Offer Fit Index describes the level of offer fit across a number of specific job factors. The index is also diagnostic—it can be disaggregated to identify those elements of a firm’s employment value proposition that are more or less aligned with the preferences of employees.
Commentary / Interpretation: Organizations typically measure offer fit using survey results. Each survey will likely have a different set of questions or methodologies for measuring offer fit.
